passages.note: House Third Reading roll call on SB1164 shows Pingerelli voted Y.

passages.provision_quote: This act does not : 1. Create or recognize a right to abortion or alter generally accepted medical standards. The Legislature does not intend this act to make lawful an abortion that is currently unlawful. 2. Repeal, by implication or otherwise, section 13-3603, Arizona Revised Statutes, or any other applicable state law regulating or restricting abortion.
passages.note: Sec. 2 Construction clause: the 15-week limit does not create/recognize a right to abortion and leaves A.R.S. 13-3603 and all other restrictions in force.

rows.reasoning: Pingerelli voted Y on SB 1164 (2022)'s House Third Reading, a gestational-limit bill permitting abortion up to 15 weeks with a medical-emergency exception, which would otherwise match the annex's rung 3 window. But the bill's Construction section states the act 'does not... [c]reate or recognize a right to abortion', does not make lawful a currently-unlawful abortion, and does not repeal section 13-3603 or any other abortion-restricting law, so per the annex's construction-clause rule the vote evidences no permitted stage and shows only the restrictive side.
